reviews.comment: Trevor Karn is the goat of calc lll for new profs and is very passionate about the subject, while he may occasionally stop in his tracks during a problem he would quickly correct himself and gave detailed explanations to new concepts or questions.
He is very caring and puts effort into the class. The class is still graded by very few tests, so you should be wary of this and prepare in advance.

He is clearly passionate about the material and capable of teaching it. The lectures did seem bland, and at times he would only setup, but not solve out entire problems. The quizzes and completed notes were only provided in class. There were three tests, each being difficult and making up a significant portion of your grade.

He would pause for 30 seconds looking at the slides almost as if this was his first time seeing the content and then he would explain it. It felt like he wasn't super confident in teaching the course but it was his first semester at A&M. Lectures didn't fell productive so I had to rely on self-learning the whole course. Go with a different prof.

He's a new professor but is very kind and you can tell he has a lot of passion for what he teaches. His lectures can get convoluted but he does a good job of working through problems and showing you how to do them yourself. Study hard for the tests because they are difficult and make up most of your grade.

Professor Karn is really interested in math but I found him to overcomplicate problems and use lots of theoretical math concepts that aren't in the homework. The homework is a much better way to learn than the lectures.

He's a new professor, so he had some trouble grading things on time at the beginning of the semester, but he got the hang of it as the class progressed. MATH251 is hard, but you can tell how passionate he is for math and that reflects in his lectures. He spends more time explaining concepts and how to set up problems and less time actually solving.

He was brand new this semester at A&M, so I was worried, but he became one of my favorite professors. Office hours helped a ton and he really did want us to succeed. The exams were somewhat challenging while he was adjusting to the course, but they became more and more fair throughout the semester. I loved this class because he made it interesting.

He's a great person. Very passionate and motivational. Exam reviews were a bit messy sometimes as were his lectures. Not very generous with credit on quizzes/exams. Probably better suited to theory/proof-based courses. I believe he WILL be a fantastic professor in the future. Make the effort to meet him where he's at, and it's easy to succeed.

Overall, decent lecturer. Talked too much while teaching and missed 2 easy quizzes. Only dropped 1 quiz grade while other profs dropped 2. Takes VERY long to grade, and graded test 2 and 3 MCQs wrong. Test averages were in the 70s, and the final was way harder than the practice exam. One of the most challenging/stressful 251 profs to take.”

My favorite math professor ever. Super accessible through office hours and email alike, so you can always get questions answered. The review materials he posts for exams are great, and make studying for tests a lot less of a headache. He is very kind and patient, and you can tell he cares for his students. I'd 100% recommend taking a class with him
